pages.text: Not all strangeness is new. Ancient bones, forgotten ruins, abandoned archives, and crystal growths may surface in unstable or chance-born Ages. They do not banish exotic wonders; often the old and impossible stand shoulder to shoulder.

Bones speak of beasts from ages before memory, and some are vast enough to make a dragon seem modest. Ruins whisper of peoples who mastered doors before we learned to knock. Archives are saddest of all, for they prove someone tried to understand.

Thus a single Age may feel both newborn and ancient: impossible geometry above, buried libraries below, and the traveler caught between wonder and archaeology with a shovel in one hand and a linking book in the other.
